newsitem.title: PERU: Peruvian poor march against rebel hostage-taking.
newsitem.headline: Peruvian poor march against rebel hostage-taking.

text.p: Thousands of Peruvians from Lima's shantytowns swarmed around the Japanese ambassador's residence on Sunday and appealed to Marxist guerrillas holding 74 hostages to free their VIP captives.
While the rebels claim they are fighting for Peru's poor, the impoverished marchers voiced strong support for President Alberto Fujimori's hard line in flatly rejecting the rebel demands.
Tupac Amaru Revolutionary Movement (MRTA) guerrillas stormed the diplomatic mansion on Dec. 17 demanding that the government free all their jailed comrades, about 400 leftist prisoners.
"Support for Fujimori. Do not give in to terrorists," shouted marchers in the crowd of 5,000 as they waved Peruvian flags and white handkerchiefs amid chants of "freedom for the hostages."

"This is a show of solidarity from the people. We want this problem to end once and for all for every one of the hostages without any of them being harmed," said Luz Jimenez, an organiser of soup kitchens in Lima's largest shantytown, Villa El Salvador.
Dressed mainly in white to symbolise peace, the marchers gathered from the dusty outskirts of Lima at a central park early on Sunday before walking two miles (three km) to the residence.
They held up placards that read: "Peru wants peace" and sang the national anthem. Brass bands played traditional Andean songs.
Neighbours along the march route draped red and white Peruvian flags from balconies, crammed upper-storey windows to applaud the protesters and joined in the singing.

"I think the people of Lima are here expressing once again their own demand -- the release of the hostages," said Juan de Dios Gavilano, mayor of one of the capital's port districts, Carmen de la Legua.
"The message to (rebel leader Nestor) Cerpa is that he does not represent anybody apart from his band of criminals. They are not guerrillas. They are simple terrorists."
Last week, Fujimori made publicity-conscious tours of Lima's shantytowns to rally support against the MRTA and what he termed their "terrorist blackmail".
